incidents.title: FIFA World Cup 2026 — Day 1 Opens (Maximum Threat Window)
incidents.location: Mexico City (opening match) / Los Angeles / New York / Dallas — National
incidents.detail: FIFA World Cup 2026 officially opens today with Mexico vs. South Africa at Estadio Azteca in Mexico City (2 PM CDT). The U.S. does not play until tomorrow, June 12 (Inglewood, CA, 9 PM ET vs. Paraguay) — but today is the maximum security posture day for the entire tournament. FBI is enforcing a zero-tolerance drone policy: unauthorized UAVs within 3 miles of any WC venue face $100,000 federal fines and criminal charges; Congress has authorized state/local law enforcement to neutralize rogue drones for the first time. FAA temporary flight restrictions (TFRs) active at all 11 U.S. host venues. DHS Secretary Mullin confirmed federal agents have already intercepted multiple TFR violations at recent test events. Controversy: U.S. denied entry to Somali referee Omar Artan citing 'vetting concerns' — Trump administration claimed derogatory information; FIFA had vetted him for 3 years. Artan returned to Somalia; FIFA confirmed his removal from the tournament. This will drive additional outrage in Muslim and African diaspora communities. AUSTIN RELEVANCE: Not a host city, but luxury hospitality threat posture elevated. Austin FC Soccer Celebration at Auditorium Shores (1.0 mi S) this evening. Enforce cyber hygiene maximum posture — WC-themed phishing and credential harvesting campaigns are confirmed active. Monitor all POS and network anomalies. Staff: do not click ANY WC-related links from unverified sources.
incidents.source: CBS News / AP / DHS / FBI / mykhel.com / USAO SDNY

incidents.title: U.S.–Iran Active War — Day 2 Strikes; Strait of Hormuz Closed
incidents.location: Iran / Bahrain / Kuwait / Jordan / Global shipping lanes
incidents.detail: ESCALATION: U.S. Central Command launched a second, larger round of airstrikes against Iran overnight (concluded ~4:30 AM Tehran time Thursday). CENTCOM confirmed 49 Tomahawk cruise missiles fired at Iranian military surveillance, communication, and air defense installations — some as close as 40 miles from Tehran. U.S. Air Force, Marines, and Navy all involved. Explosions heard in Tehran, Bandar Abbas, Qeshm, Minab, and Sirik. Iran retaliated against U.S. Fifth Fleet (Bahrain), U.S. airbase in Jordan, and Kuwait for a second consecutive night. Kuwait temporarily closed its airspace; Bahrain activated missile alert systems. Iran declared the Strait of Hormuz closed to all vessels including oil tankers — CENTCOM disputes this claim but oil prices are surging. Israel activated shelter alerts in northern Israel amid reports of potential incoming fire from Lebanon. UN Secretary-General Guterres called the ceasefire a 'lesser-fire.' Trump: 'We negotiate with bombs.' Defense Secretary Hegseth: CENTCOM would 'be busy tonight.' AUSTIN RELEVANCE (HIGH): Iranian diaspora community is at maximum tension. Iran's WC team is in Tijuana — Iran plays June 15 in LA. Brief all staff: avoid any geopolitical commentary with guests. Log any unusual inquiries about Middle East military operations. Oil price spike may affect travel and logistics planning. Cyber threat: Iranian state-sponsored groups have a history of retaliatory cyber operations against U.S. targets during armed conflict periods.
incidents.source: NYT Live Updates / AP / Al Jazeera / CNN

Monitor Capitol/Congress Ave and UT campus. Combined with today's FIFA WC opening and U.S.-Iran conflict, the overall emotional temperature of large crowds throughout Austin is elevated. Brief all staff on de-escalation.
